sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Natalie Kittroweth.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的娜塔莉·基特罗韦斯。

sentences.en: This is The Daily on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 这是《周日日报》。

sentences.en: It's the middle of August, and that can mean only one thing.
sentences.zh: 现在是八月中旬，这意味着只有一件事。

sentences.en: Across the country, people are popping open their beach chairs, digging their umbrellas into the sand, and settling in to their favorite books.
sentences.zh: 全国各地的人们都撑开了沙滩椅，把遮阳伞插进沙子里，安顿下来阅读他们最喜欢的书。

sentences.en: And of all the literary genres to bring with you on vacation, for me and millions of Americans, there's one that stands above the reSt.
sentences.zh: 在所有适合度假时携带的文学类型中，对我以及数百万美国人来说，有一种类型脱颖而出。

sentences.en: And that is the thriller.
sentences.zh: 那就是惊悚小说。

sentences.en: Thrillers dominate bestseller lists.
sentences.zh: 惊悚小说占据了畅销书榜单。

sentences.en: They get adapted into hit movies.
sentences.zh: 它们被改编成热门电影。

sentences.en: They don't let you put them down.
sentences.zh: 它们让你爱不释手。

sentences.en: And so, this month, our colleagues at The Book Review released their list of the 50 best thrillers of the century.
sentences.zh: 因此，本月，我们在《书评》的同事发布了他们评选的本世纪50部最佳惊悚小说榜单。

sentences.en: Today, I speak with our in-house expert on the thriller genre, reporter Sarah Lyle, and also the great author Tana French, who has four books on this liSt.
sentences.zh: 今天，我将与我们的内部惊悚小说专家、记者莎拉·莱尔，以及伟大的作家塔娜·法兰奇交谈，她的四本书入选了这份榜单。

sentences.en: It's Sunday, August 16th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月16日，星期日。

sentences.en: Sarah, you are our resident expert on thrillers here at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 莎拉，你是我们《纽约时报》的常驻惊悚小说专家。

sentences.en: You have a monthly column on the genre for our book section, and I think of you as my personal encyclopedia, because this is my favorite kind of book.
sentences.zh: 你为我们的书评版块撰写关于该类型的月度专栏，我把你视为我的个人百科全书，因为这是我最喜欢的书的类型。

sentences.en: Always has been.
sentences.zh: 一直都是。

sentences.en: Always will be.
sentences.zh: 永远都会是。

sentences.en: I actually have a group of friends at The Times that feels the same, and we've done this thing
sentences.zh: 其实我在《时报》有一群朋友也有同感，我们做过一件事，

sentences.en: where we deputize one person to write to you and ask for your personal recommendations for must-reads.
sentences.zh: 就是指派一个人写信给你，询问你个人推荐的必读书目。

sentences.en: We will read anything you say.
sentences.zh: 你说什么我们都会读。

sentences.en: You are our leader.
sentences.zh: 你是我们的领袖。

sentences.en: So, welcome to the Sunday Daily.
sentences.zh: 那么，欢迎来到《周日日报》。

sentences.en: Okay, that's a huge responsibility, but I will do my beSt.
sentences.zh: 好的，这责任重大，但我会尽我所能。

sentences.en: It's great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Okay, I want to get to this massive and fascinating list that you all just put together of the best thrillers of the century.
sentences.zh: 好的，我想谈谈你们刚刚整理出的这份庞大而迷人的本世纪最佳惊悚小说榜单。

sentences.en: But before we do, can you please just give me a baseline?
sentences.zh: 但在我们开始之前，你能先给我一个基准吗？

sentences.en: What defines a thriller in your mind?
sentences.zh: 在你心目中，什么定义了惊悚小说？

sentences.en: Well, I think, as you say, it's a pretty personal understanding.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想正如你所说，这是一种非常个人的理解。

sentences.en: There's no real definition of a thriller.
sentences.zh: 惊悚小说并没有真正的定义。

sentences.en: But I would say, at the heart, it has to have a lot of suspense.
sentences.zh: 但我会说，核心在于它必须有很强的悬疑感。

sentences.en: It has to have a plot that moves you along.
sentences.zh: 它必须有一个推动你前进的情节。

sentences.en: You have to be dying to find out what happened.
sentences.zh: 你必须迫不及待地想知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: And what about the mystery element?
sentences.zh: 那神秘元素呢？

sentences.en: Is that a necessity?
sentences.zh: 那是必须的吗？

sentences.en: Well, mystery is a very broad term.
sentences.zh: 嗯，神秘是一个非常宽泛的词。

sentences.en: And in some sense, sort of any book that you really love, there's some sort of thriller mystery element in it.
sentences.zh: 在某种意义上，你真正喜欢的任何书，里面都有某种惊悚或神秘的元素。

sentences.en: I mean, is Charlotte going to be able to save Wilbur, for example?
sentences.zh: 我是说，比如夏洛特能救下威尔伯吗？

sentences.en: That's a great mystery.
sentences.zh: 那是个伟大的谜题。

sentences.en: From Charlotte's Web.
sentences.zh: 出自《夏洛的网》。

sentences.en: From Charlotte's Web, yeah.
sentences.zh: 出自《夏洛的网》，没错。

sentences.en: Fair enough.
sentences.zh: 有道理。

sentences.en: Okay, so what's your origin story with the genre?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么你与这种类型的渊源是什么？

sentences.en: Like, how'd you get into it?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么接触到它的？

sentences.en: So I think like a lot of neglected children of the 1970s and early 80s, I was left alone in houses with random books that people would leave there.
sentences.zh: 我想就像70年代和80年代初许多被忽视的孩子一样，我被独自留在屋子里，读着别人留在那里的各种书。

sentences.en: And I have to say, though, I did probably start with Nancy Drew.
sentences.zh: 不过我必须说，我大概是从《南茜·朱鲁》开始的。

sentences.en: Like, a lot of people, you know, there's so many of those books.
sentences.zh: 就像很多人一样，你知道，那些书实在太多了。

sentences.en: It's where I learned a lot of vocabulary words.
sentences.zh: 我在那里学到了很多词汇。

sentences.en: I learned what secluded means.
sentences.zh: 我学会了“与世隔绝”是什么意思。

sentences.en: For years, I thought that deceased meant dying of some awful disease.
sentences.zh: 多年来，我一直以为“去世”是指死于某种可怕的疾病。

sentences.en: Like, I didn't realize it was just dying.
sentences.zh: 我没意识到它只是指死亡。

sentences.en: And then I graduated to Agatha Christie's, which often seemed to be in a lot of these houses.
sentences.zh: 后来我升级到了阿加莎·克里斯蒂的作品，这些书似乎经常出现在这些房子里。

sentences.en: And it was some time before my mom told me you didn't pronounce Agatha Agatha.
sentences.zh: 过了很久我妈妈才告诉我，阿加莎的名字不是那样读的。

sentences.en: And then when I was probably in fifth or sixth grade, there was this book called The Silver Crown by Robert C.
sentences.zh: 后来大概在我五年级或六年级的时候，有一本叫《银冠》的书，作者是罗伯特·C·奥布莱恩，一位伟大的儿童作家。

sentences.en: O'Brien, a great children's writer.
sentences.zh: 我朋友米歇尔有一本。

sentences.en: And my friend Michelle had one copy of it.
sentences.zh: 我们在她父母旅行车的后座上，周末过后在夜里从科德角开车回纽约，手里拿着手电筒。

sentences.en: And we were in the back of her parents' station wagon, driving from Cape Cod to New York at night after some weekend with a flashlight.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都迫切地想知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: And we were both, like, desperate to find out what happened.
sentences.zh: 我们每人读一章，然后很不情愿地把它交给对方。

sentences.en: And we'd each read a chapter and then unwillingly hand it over to the other person.
sentences.zh: 我读的速度大概是她的三倍。

sentences.en: And I read, like, three times as quickly as she did.
sentences.zh: 我说，快点。

sentences.en: And I'm like, hurry up.
sentences.zh: 我们当时在吃巧克力豆饼干。

sentences.en: And we were eating chocolate chip cookies.
sentences.zh: 那真是太不可思议了。

sentences.en: And it was so incredible.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一种发自内心的体验。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a visceral experience.
sentences.zh: 这是一种发自内心的体验。

sentences.en: It's a visceral experience.
sentences.zh: 你简直是如饥似渴地在读这本书。

sentences.en: You were literally ravenous for the book.
sentences.zh: 你在“吃”掉它。

sentences.en: You're eating it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是它在“吃”掉你。

sentences.en: Well, it's eating you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其中一些书，我记得我第一次读《无罪推定》时，因为我当时在上班。

sentences.en: And, you know, with some of them, like, I remember when I first read Presumed Innocent, because I was at work.
sentences.zh: 我试着把它放在膝盖上读，这样老板就不会看到我没在工作。

sentences.en: I was trying to read it on my lap so my boss wouldn't see that I wasn't working.
sentences.zh: 我一直在读。

sentences.en: And I was reading.
sentences.zh: 我试着在晚上回家的出租车上读它。

sentences.en: I tried to read it in the taxi on the way home at night.
sentences.zh: 我想我整晚都没睡。

sentences.en: And I stayed up, I think, all night.
sentences.zh: 整晚。

sentences.en: All night.
sentences.zh: 因为我太想知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: Because I wanted so much to find out what happened.
sentences.zh: 是的，当你真正沉浸在这些书中时，这就是它们的全部意义所在，它们抓住了你。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's something that when you're really into these books, which is the whole point of them, they grip you.
sentences.zh: 它们让你无法自拔。

sentences.en: They don't let you go.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像你和这本书有某种不正当的关系，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It feels almost like you're having this, like, illicit relationship with this thing, you know?
sentences.zh: 你在藏着它。

sentences.en: You're hiding it.
sentences.zh: 它正在接管你的生活。

sentences.en: It's taking over you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它也让世界上的其他事物相比之下显得非常苍白。

sentences.en: Well, it's also, it makes the rest of the world seem very pale in comparison.
sentences.zh: 你读完后会有点颤抖，有点疲惫，就像你刚吸了某种毒品，而其他人都不理解。

sentences.en: And you sort of finish a little bit shaky, a little bit tired, sort of like you were on some kind of drug and no one else understands.
sentences.zh: 你试着告诉他们你为什么喜欢它。

sentences.en: And you try to tell them why you loved it.
sentences.zh: 他们却说，安静点。

sentences.en: And they're like, be quiet.
sentences.zh: 别剧透。

sentences.en: Don't give it away.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 而且他们可能不会像你那样喜欢它。

sentences.en: And they probably won't love it as much as you do.
sentences.zh: 那会非常令人失望。

sentences.en: And then that's very disappointing.
sentences.zh: 那么我们来谈谈这50部最佳作品的榜单吧。

sentences.en: So let's talk about the 50 best, this liSt.
sentences.zh: 《时报》发布了很多这样的榜单。

sentences.en: The Times puts out a lot of lists like this.
sentences.zh: 而这一份对我来说，我知道我会把它保存在电脑的书签里，一遍又一遍地反复阅读。

sentences.en: And this is the one for me where I knew that I was just going to keep it bookmarked on my computer and go back to it again and again and again.
sentences.zh: 所以我的问题是，你是如何对过去26年里的前50部惊悚小说进行排名的？

sentences.en: So my question is, how do you go about ranking the top 50 thrillers in the last 26 years?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们《时报书评》的做法是向各种各样的惊悚小说作家发送了大量的选票，

sentences.en: Well, what we at the Times Book Review did was send out a lot of ballots to a really wide range of writers of different sorts of thrillers,
sentences.zh: 你知道，包括警察办案类、心理惊悚类、科幻作家、图书博主、编辑、出版商等。

sentences.en: you know, police procedurals, psychological thrillers, science fiction writers, book influencers, editors, publishers.
sentences.zh: 我们邀请他们每人列出自己的前10名，并以此为基础得出了我们的榜单。

sentences.en: And we invited each of them to list their top 10 and came up with our list based on that.
sentences.zh: 唯一的提示是它们必须写于这个新世纪，所以2000年之前的作品不包括在内。

sentences.en: And the only prompt was they had to be written in this new century, so nothing before 2000.
sentences.zh: 我们没有定义什么是惊悚小说，所以人们可以把他们想要的任何书放进榜单，

sentences.en: And we didn't define thriller, so people were able to put what they wanted on the list,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们榜单上的一些书，就像我们刚才谈到的《夏洛的网》一样，

sentences.en: which is why some of the books on our list, people, just as we were talking about with Charlotte's Web, for example,
sentences.zh: 它们不会出现在书店或图书馆的惊悚小说区，但它们确实包含令人难以置信的惊悚元素。

sentences.en: they wouldn't be in the thriller section of the bookstore or the library, but they have incredible thriller elements in them.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈共识度最高的那本书，也就是榜单上的第一名，《消失的爱人》。

sentences.en: Let's talk about the book about which there was the most consensus, which is the number one book on the list, Gone Girl.
sentences.zh: 这本由吉莉安·弗琳创作的广受欢迎的心理惊悚小说，是在十多年前出版的。

sentences.en: This massively popular psychological thriller by Gillian Flynn came out a little more than 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 它被改编成了由本·阿弗莱克主演的大电影。

sentences.en: It was made into this big movie with Ben Affleck.
sentences.zh: 你感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: Were you surprised?
sentences.zh: 我不知道，这太有趣了。

sentences.en: I don't know, it's so interesting.
sentences.zh: 如果你查看我们的网站，你还可以找到许多著名作家给我们的选票。

sentences.en: So if you look on our website, you can also find the ballots that a bunch of famous authors gave us.
sentences.zh: 每一份榜单，除了可能一两份之外，都包含了《消失的爱人》。

sentences.en: Every single list, with the exception of maybe one or two, had Gone Girl on it.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢它，我并不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And I'm not surprised that people loved it.
sentences.zh: 悬念简直令人难以置信。

sentences.en: The suspense is unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 它拥有书中最美味的一组不可靠叙述者。

sentences.en: It has one of the most delicious sets of unreliable narrators ever used in a book.
sentences.zh: 故事讲的是一个女人失踪了，也就是这个男人的妻子。

sentences.en: So it's about a woman who disappears, this guy's wife.
sentences.zh: 她叙述了其中的一部分，他叙述了其中的一部分，还有一部分是通过她的日记叙述的。

sentences.en: And she narrates parts of it, he narrates parts of it, and parts of it are narrated by her journal.
sentences.zh: 这三者都是不可靠的。

sentences.en: All three of those things are unreliable.
sentences.zh: 你无法信任他们中的任何一个。

sentences.en: You can't trust any of them.
sentences.zh: 在早期的章节中有一个惊人的时刻，丈夫正在接受警察关于他妻子突然失踪的审讯。

sentences.en: There's an amazing moment in one of the early chapters where the husband is being interrogated by the cops about the sudden disappearance of his wife.
sentences.zh: 他正在告诉我们发生了什么以及他说了什么。

sentences.en: And he is telling us what happened and what he said.
sentences.zh: 而在那一章的结尾，他说了一些类似这样的话：这是我向警察撒的第五个谎，而我才刚刚开始。

sentences.en: And at the end of the chapter, he says something like, it was the fifth lie I had told the police, and I was only just beginning.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 你会想，这些事情里哪一个是谎言？

sentences.en: And you're like, which of these things was a lie?
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么榜单上还有哪些书看起来是自然入选的，大家都同意的？

sentences.en: Okay, and what are the other books on this list that seem like natural fits that made it, that everyone agreed on?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们谈论的是那些成为畅销书并引发全国讨论的书。

sentences.en: Well, I think we're talking about books that were bestsellers that sort of hit the national conversation.
sentences.zh: 其中许多，如果不是全部的话，都被改编成了电影或电视剧。

sentences.en: And many of them, if not all the ones in that category, were made into movies or TV shows.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上增强了它们的知名度。

sentences.en: So that sort of enhanced their visibility.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会说斯蒂格·拉森的《龙纹身的女孩》排在第四位。

sentences.en: So we'd say The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo by Stig Larson coming in at number four.
sentences.zh: 米克·赫伦的《流人》，Apple TV系列剧。

sentences.en: Slow Horses by Mick Heron, Apple TV series.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它。

sentences.en: Love it.
sentences.zh: 宝拉·霍金斯的《火车上的女孩》。

sentences.en: The Girl on the Train by Paula Hawkins.
sentences.zh: 《达芬奇密码》。

sentences.en: The Da Vinci Code.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Classic.
sentences.zh: 经典之作。

sentences.en: Big Little Lies.
sentences.zh: 《大小谎言》。

sentences.en: You know, there's a whole bunch of them that everybody would have heard the titles and possibly seen the TV show, movie, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这其中有很多书，大家可能都听过书名，甚至看过改编的电视剧、电影等等。

sentences.en: Any big surprises?
sentences.zh: 有什么大惊喜吗？

sentences.en: Are there books on this list that you just wouldn't have been able to predict going in?
sentences.zh: 这份书单里有没有哪本书是你一开始完全没料到会入选的？

sentences.en: There are quite a few books on this list that wouldn't be considered a traditional classic or even defined as a thriller.
sentences.zh: 书单里有不少书，它们并不被视为传统经典，甚至都算不上惊悚小说。

sentences.en: And I was struck that enough people voted for these non-thriller thrillers that they made it to the liSt.
sentences.zh: 让我感到惊讶的是，竟然有这么多人为这些“非惊悚类的惊悚小说”投票，让它们成功入选。

sentences.en: And for example, The Sympathizer, which won the Pulitzer Prize a few years back, which is an incredible novel about a spy,
sentences.zh: 比如几年前获得普利策奖的《同情者》，那是一部关于间谍的精彩小说，

sentences.en: but also about the experience of Vietnamese people in the United States.
sentences.zh: 但它同时也讲述了越南人在美国的生活经历。

sentences.en: I mean, it's high literature, but it has a great mystery in it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它是高水准的文学作品，但其中又包含了一个很棒的悬疑故事。

sentences.en: Room by Emma Donoghue, which is a book about essentially a child who's been raised in captivity.
sentences.zh: 艾玛·多诺霍的《房间》，这本书本质上讲的是一个在囚禁中长大的孩子。

sentences.en: And it's, again, an incredible book about a family and maternal love, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 同样，这是一部关于家庭、母爱等等的杰作。

sentences.en: But it's – and so you wouldn't really think of it as a thriller.
sentences.zh: 但它——你真的不会把它看作是一部惊悚小说。

sentences.en: That's on the list as well.
sentences.zh: 但它也出现在了这份书单上。

sentences.en: Another one that I was really happy to see on the list, although slightly surprised because it's not a traditional thriller, is The Goldfinch by Donna Tartt,
sentences.zh: 另一本让我很高兴看到入选，尽管有点惊讶，因为它也不是传统的惊悚小说，那就是唐娜·塔特的《金翅雀》，

sentences.en: which starts in a thrillery way.
sentences.zh: 它的开头确实很有惊悚片的味道。

sentences.en: An explosion at a museum, a missing painting, and then in real Tartt fashion turns into something much bigger than the sum of its parts.
sentences.zh: 博物馆爆炸、名画失踪，然后以典型的塔特风格，演变成了一部远超其情节本身的作品。

sentences.en: But most people, if you just mentioned that book, would say literature.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人如果提到这本书，会说它是文学作品。

sentences.en: They wouldn't say thriller.
sentences.zh: 他们不会说它是惊悚小说。

sentences.en: So it's very exciting to see it on here.
sentences.zh: 所以能在这里看到它非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: Speaking of great literature, I've always felt just the smallest amount of, I don't know, sheepish about the fact that this is my favorite genre, thrillers, mysteries.
sentences.zh: 说到伟大的文学作品，我一直对“惊悚和悬疑”是我最喜欢的类型这件事，感到有一点点……怎么说呢，不好意思。

sentences.en: I think because when people think of these books, they tend to think of airport paperbacks, of pulp.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为当人们想到这些书时，往往会想到机场书店里的平装书，想到通俗读物。

sentences.en: I think there are people who see them as formulaic.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有些人认为它们是套路化的。

sentences.en: Murder happens, police procedural begins, payoff comes with everything being solved at the end.
sentences.zh: 发生谋杀案，警察开始办案，最后一切真相大白。

sentences.en: But looking at this list, you see that there's just this really wide variety within the genre itself.
sentences.zh: 但看看这份书单，你会发现这个类型本身其实非常多元。

sentences.en: These kinds of books can be incredibly literary and well-written.
sentences.zh: 这类书完全可以写得极具文学性，文笔优美。

sentences.en: Well, first of all, you shouldn't be embarrassed about any book you read.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，你不应该为你读的任何书感到尴尬。

sentences.en: It's so great to read.
sentences.zh: 阅读本身就是一件很棒的事。

sentences.en: People should read more.
sentences.zh: 人们应该多读书。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Note taken.
sentences.zh: 记下了。

sentences.en: And, of course, the thriller genre is so expansive.
sentences.zh: 而且，惊悚小说这个类型当然是非常宽泛的。

sentences.en: It can be police procedural.
sentences.zh: 它可以是警察办案类。

sentences.en: It can be science fiction.
sentences.zh: 可以是科幻类。

sentences.en: It can be psychological thriller.
sentences.zh: 可以是心理惊悚类。

sentences.en: And the best ones are the ones that marry, you know, those thriller-ish elements with, like, beautiful writing.
sentences.zh: 而最棒的作品，往往是将那些惊悚元素与优美的文笔完美结合在一起的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So can you give us some examples of books on this list that do that for you, that are that perfect marriage of literature and plot?
sentences.zh: 那么你能给我们举几个书单上符合这一点的例子吗？就是那种文学性和情节完美结合的作品？

sentences.en: There's a bunch of them, and it's really exciting to see them there.
sentences.zh: 有很多这样的书，能看到它们入选真的很令人兴奋。

sentences.en: And the first I'd mention is Case Histories by Kate Atkinson.
sentences.zh: 我首先要提的是凯特·阿特金森的《案中案》。

sentences.en: All-timer.
sentences.zh: 永恒的经典。

sentences.en: All-timer.
sentences.zh: 绝对的经典。

sentences.en: Again, it's not a conventional thriller, really, although it's sort of billed as a detective novel.
sentences.zh: 同样，它不是一部传统的惊悚小说，尽管它被归类为侦探小说。

sentences.en: And it's nominally about a guy called Jackson Brody, who's a former cop.
sentences.zh: 名义上它是关于一个叫杰克逊·布罗迪的前警察的故事。

sentences.en: And he's called on to try to solve three or four, I think it is, impossible cold cases that all involve heartbreak with children dying and people's relatives dying.
sentences.zh: 他受命去解决三四个——我想是三四个——不可能完成的悬案，这些案子都涉及孩子夭折和亲人离世的悲剧。

sentences.en: And how he goes about it, how she plunges you inside of these different stories, but also into the story of him.
sentences.zh: 她处理这些故事的方式，她将你带入这些不同故事，以及他个人故事的方式，都非常出色。

sentences.en: One more that I was so happy to see on here was The Plot by Gene Hemp Corlett, which is a super clever mystery that works on so many different levels, including the title,
sentences.zh: 还有一本我也很高兴看到入选的是吉恩·汉普·科莱特的《情节》，这是一部超级聪明的悬疑小说，在多个层面上都很出色，包括书名，

sentences.en: which does double service.
sentences.zh: 书名本身就有一语双关的效果。

sentences.en: It's about a professor of literature at some awful junior college who's now an unsuccessful writer who steals someone else's plot and produces a book based on it.
sentences.zh: 故事讲的是某所糟糕的社区学院的一位文学教授，他是一个失败的作家，偷了别人的情节并据此写了一本书。

sentences.en: But that's not really what it's about, necessarily.
sentences.zh: 但这并不完全是它的核心内容。

sentences.en: It's about multiple thefts of different sorts of things, and it's great.
sentences.zh: 它涉及多种不同层面的窃取，非常棒。

sentences.en: But by far, my favorite on this list, and someone who I was very happy to see has four books on the list, is Tana French, the great Irish author.
sentences.zh: 但到目前为止，我在这份书单上最喜欢的，而且我很高兴看到她有四本书入选的作者，是伟大的爱尔兰作家塔娜·法兰奇。

sentences.en: The goat.
sentences.zh: GOAT（史上最佳）。

sentences.en: Some of us call her the goat of greatest of all time.
sentences.zh: 我们有些人称她为“史上最佳”。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Tana French has four books on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 所以塔娜·法兰奇有四本书入选了书单。

sentences.en: In the Woods at number three, Broken Harbor at number 20, The Witch Elm at number 33, and The Likeness at number 34.
sentences.zh: 《神秘森林》排在第三，《破碎港》排在第20，《巫榆园》排在第33，《相似者》排在第34。

sentences.en: All amazing.
sentences.zh: 都很棒。

sentences.en: All amazing.
sentences.zh: 都很棒。

sentences.en: And the first one she ever wrote, which is number three, is In the Woods, which many people feel is the beSt.
sentences.zh: 她写的第一本书，也就是排在第三的《神秘森林》，很多人认为那是她最好的作品。

sentences.en: I remember reading that when I was a London correspondent and just being mesmerized by the several mysteries flowing through it, by the writing, by the characters,
sentences.zh: 我记得我在担任伦敦通讯员时读过那本书，被书中交织的几个悬疑点、文笔、人物塑造深深吸引，

sentences.en: by the stuff that she revealed along the way, by the police investigation.
sentences.zh: 还有她一路揭示的线索，以及警察的调查过程。

sentences.en: Oh, my goodness.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: What a book.
sentences.zh: 真是本好书。

sentences.en: And what's your sense, Sarah, of the broad appeal of Tana French?
sentences.zh: 莎拉，你觉得塔娜·法兰奇的广泛吸引力来自哪里？

sentences.en: Why is it that so many people agree about just how good she is?
sentences.zh: 为什么这么多人对她的作品评价如此之高？

sentences.en: I thought she was sort of my little special secret.
sentences.zh: 我原以为她只是我个人的小秘密。

sentences.en: So I was gratified and happy to see how broad the consensus is that she's so great.
sentences.zh: 所以看到大家对她评价如此之高，我感到非常欣慰和高兴。

sentences.en: And honestly, I think it goes back to what we were talking about before, of what makes the absolute best thriller, which is not just the plot at all.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我认为这又回到了我们之前讨论的话题，即什么才是最顶级的惊悚小说，它绝不仅仅是情节。

sentences.en: It combines incredible plot pacing with beautiful writing, characterizations, a sense of the people, their psychology, their relationships, and like all great literature,
sentences.zh: 它将令人难以置信的情节节奏与优美的文笔、人物刻画、对人物及其心理、人际关系的深刻洞察结合在一起，就像所有伟大的文学作品一样，

sentences.en: truths about being human.
sentences.zh: 揭示了关于人性的真理。

sentences.en: Okay, you've talked to Tana French many times.
sentences.zh: 好的，你采访过塔娜·法兰奇很多次了。

sentences.en: What would you ask her if you were, you know, in the position of interviewing her for the Sunday Daily?
sentences.zh: 如果你有机会在《周日日报》采访她，你会问她什么？

sentences.en: Um, I want to know what she's writing next.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想知道她下一部写什么。

sentences.en: That's all I really care about.
sentences.zh: 这是我唯一关心的。

sentences.en: Why hasn't it been published yet?
sentences.zh: 为什么还没出版？

sentences.en: When can we read it?
sentences.zh: 我们什么时候能读到？

sentences.en: Could you write a little faster, please?
sentences.zh: 能不能写快一点，拜托？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Without compromising your quality.
sentences.zh: 当然是在保证质量的前提下。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, Sarah, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 那么，莎拉，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: It's been wonderful having you here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来。

sentences.en: This was really fun.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: After the break, I talk to Tana French.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我将采访塔娜·法兰奇。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《Connections》谜题，我热爱恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，也喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫“联觉”的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像刚才那几位一样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏吧。

sentences.en: Tana French, welcome to the Sunday Daily.
sentences.zh: 塔娜·法兰奇，欢迎来到《周日日报》。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me on.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: This is extremely cool.
sentences.zh: 这太酷了。

sentences.en: So just to put my cards on the table, I have read every word that you've written.
sentences.zh: 先摊牌一下，你写的每一个字我都读过。

sentences.en: So for me, when the Times list of the 50 best thrillers of the century came out, it was not surprising that you had four books on there.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，当《纽约时报》发布“世纪最佳惊悚小说50强”榜单时，你有四本书入选一点也不让我惊讶。

sentences.en: I am so over the moon about that.
sentences.zh: 我对此感到欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: It's the coolest thing.
sentences.zh: 这真是太酷了。

sentences.en: You've developed, I'm sure you know, quite a cult-like following.
sentences.zh: 我想你也知道，你已经拥有了一批狂热的追随者。

sentences.en: I learned in preparing for this interview that it's not just me.
sentences.zh: 我在准备这次采访时发现，不仅仅是我一个人这样。

sentences.en: There's a whole online community of people who feel this deep emptiness after finishing one of your books and who also pre-order you as soon as humanly possible.
sentences.zh: 网上有一个庞大的读者群体，他们在读完你的书后会感到深深的空虚，而且一有新书就会第一时间预订。

sentences.en: When you are writing, who do you think you are writing for and what do you think that person wants out of one of your books?
sentences.zh: 当你写作时，你认为你在为谁写？你觉得那个人想从你的书中得到什么？

sentences.en: I can't think in those terms because I figure that readers are so varied, so diverse, that if I start thinking in those terms, I'm just going to get confused, start overthinking,
sentences.zh: 我无法从那个角度去思考，因为我觉得读者群体太广泛、太多样了，如果我开始那样想，我只会感到困惑，开始过度思考，

sentences.en: and nothing will ever come out right.
sentences.zh: 最后什么也写不出来。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I'm thinking always in terms of the book, the characters, the story, what is right for those.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是从书本身、人物、故事出发，思考什么对它们来说是正确的。

sentences.en: Whoever's reading my books has a certain amount in common with me and what they like to read, what they like to think about, what they're interested in.
sentences.zh: 无论谁在读我的书，他们和我都有一定的共同点，比如喜欢读什么、喜欢思考什么、对什么感兴趣。

sentences.en: So I have to just take on trust that if I write this book as well as I'm humanly capable of and try to do justice to the characters, the story, the themes,
sentences.zh: 所以我必须相信，如果我尽我所能写好这本书，并努力对人物、故事和主题负责，

sentences.en: then that will strike some chord with the readers.
sentences.zh: 那么它就会引起读者的共鸣。

sentences.en: That's the only way I can do it.
sentences.zh: 这是我唯一能做到的方式。

sentences.en: Meaning if you're enjoying yourself writing it, if you're having fun, if it's gripping you, you assume that will be the effect for others.
sentences.zh: 意思是如果你自己在写作时感到享受，感到有趣，被故事吸引，你就会假设其他人也会有同样的感受。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And if it's striking that chord where you know where you're reading something and it just feels right, you're going, yes, that is the right note for the character.
sentences.zh: 如果它触动了那个共鸣点，让你觉得读起来感觉对了，你会想：没错，这就是这个人物该有的感觉。

sentences.en: The plot is coming together right.
sentences.zh: 情节发展得恰到好处。

sentences.en: That just feels, it's got that true note.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉，就是有一种真实感。

sentences.en: If I'm feeling that, then hopefully the people who like my books will feel that way too.
sentences.zh: 如果我有这种感觉，那么希望喜欢我书的人也会有同样的感受。

sentences.en: How did you come to this work in the first place?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么开始从事这份工作的？

sentences.en: Kind of accidentally.
sentences.zh: 算是偶然吧。

sentences.en: Like I wrote a lot when I was a kid.
sentences.zh: 我小时候写过很多东西。

sentences.en: That was definitely one of my plans, but I sidetracked off into acting.
sentences.zh: 那确实是我的计划之一，但我后来转行去做了演员。

sentences.en: But, you know, acting.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，演戏嘛。

sentences.en: The gigs never line up neatly unless you're a Judi Dench or somebody, which I definitely was not.
sentences.zh: 除非你是朱迪·丹奇那样的大腕，否则工作机会从来都不稳定，而我显然不是。

sentences.en: And I had some time off between two shows and I've always loved archaeology.
sentences.zh: 我在两部戏之间有段空档期，我一直很喜欢考古学。

sentences.en: I've always been fascinated.
sentences.zh: 我一直对此很着迷。

sentences.en: So I went, right, I'm going to get myself a few weeks work on an archaeological dig.
sentences.zh: 所以我心想，好吧，我要去参加一个考古挖掘工作，干几周。

sentences.en: Very cool, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这很酷。

sentences.en: It really was.
sentences.zh: 确实很酷。

sentences.en: It was so much fun.
sentences.zh: 真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: But one day there was a wood near the dig and I was looking at it going, that would be a really cool place for kids to play.
sentences.zh: 但有一天，挖掘现场附近有一片树林，我看着它想，那对孩子们来说是个玩耍的好地方。

sentences.en: And instead of stopping there, like a normal person, I did the mystery writer thing of always looking for the mystery in everything, which is, I think,
sentences.zh: 我没有像正常人那样就此打住，而是发挥了悬疑小说家的本能，总是试图在任何事物中寻找悬疑点，我认为，

sentences.en: one of the marks of a mystery writer.
sentences.zh: 这是悬疑小说家的标志之一。

sentences.en: And I went, well, what if three kids ran in there to play and only one ever came out and he had no memory of what had happened to the other two?
sentences.zh: 我心想，如果三个孩子跑进去玩，只有一个出来了，而且他不记得另外两个发生了什么，会怎样？

sentences.en: And then what if he grew up to be a detective and a case drew him back to that wood and he's there knowing that the solution to the mystery is in his mind, but he can't find it.
sentences.zh: 如果他长大后成为了一名侦探，而一个案件又把他带回了那片树林，他身处其中，知道谜底就在他脑海里，但他却找不到，会怎样？

sentences.en: And I realized that, I mean, I really wanted to know what would happen and no one else was going to write it for me.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，我是真的很想知道会发生什么，而且没有别人会为我写出来。

sentences.en: So I hadn't tried to write a book before, so I figured I probably couldn't,
sentences.zh: 我以前从没试过写书，所以我以为我可能写不出来，

sentences.en: but I could write a scene and then another scene and suddenly I had a chapter and suddenly I realized I was taking this really,
sentences.zh: 但我可以写一个场景，然后再写一个场景，突然间我就有了一章，突然间我意识到我开始非常、

sentences.en: really seriously and turning down acting work for it, which is a big deal.
sentences.zh: 非常认真地对待这件事，甚至为此推掉了演艺工作，这可是件大事。

sentences.en: And here we all are, like 20 years later.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就到了这里，20年过去了。

sentences.en: That's obviously the premise of In the Woods, your first book, which was number three on this liSt.
sentences.zh: 那显然就是你第一本书《神秘森林》的前提，它在书单上排第三。

sentences.en: How did the novel grow from that original kernel of an idea?
sentences.zh: 这部小说是如何从最初那个核心创意发展起来的？

sentences.en: I know you're saying you put scene after scene after scene together, but walk me through your process.
sentences.zh: 我知道你说你是把一个接一个的场景拼凑起来的，但能带我了解一下你的创作过程吗？

sentences.en: Did you know what was going to happen at the end?
sentences.zh: 你当时知道结局会是什么样吗？

sentences.en: How did you get there?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么写到那里的？

sentences.en: It was messy.
sentences.zh: 过程很混乱。

sentences.en: I've got to say, it still is.
sentences.zh: 我得说，现在依然很混乱。

sentences.en: My process is still really, really messy, but that was the first time I'd ever written a book, so it was much messier.
sentences.zh: 我的创作过程依然非常、非常混乱，但那是我第一次写书，所以当时要混乱得多。

sentences.en: I had no idea.
sentences.zh: 我完全没头绪。

sentences.en: I had a really strong sense of the setting and of the character.
sentences.zh: 我对故事背景和角色有着非常强烈的感知。

sentences.en: This guy who was really damaged at that crucial point in his life, you know, you're 12, you're just forming who you are.
sentences.zh: 这个人在人生的关键时刻受到了严重的创伤，你知道，那时你才12岁，正是人格形成的阶段。

sentences.en: And there was this huge crack through his life and his perception of himself and his relationship with his own mind.
sentences.zh: 他的生活，他对自我的认知，以及他与自己内心的关系，从此出现了一道巨大的裂痕。

sentences.en: And so this guy who is now 20 years later, who's a grown-up, but that crack is still running through everything he does.
sentences.zh: 所以，20年后的他虽然已经是个成年人，但那道裂痕依然贯穿于他所做的一切之中。

sentences.en: I had a really strong sense of him and of this place and this basic premise.
sentences.zh: 我对这个人物、这个地方以及这个基本前提有着非常强烈的感知。

sentences.en: And from there, I was winging it.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我就全靠临场发挥了。

sentences.en: I was figuring out who he was, how he would relate to the case, how he would relate to, you know, the other character, Cassie, his partner and best friend, came up fairly quickly.
sentences.zh: 我一边写一边摸索他是谁，他会如何处理案件，他会如何与其他人相处，比如他的搭档兼挚友凯西（Cassie），这个角色很快就浮现出来了。

sentences.en: So what would their relationship be like?
sentences.zh: 那么，他们的关系会是什么样的呢？

sentences.en: And what would this sort of dark fault line through him do to everything from the investigation to the friendship to the way he engaged with this old case surfacing?
sentences.zh: 而他内心那道黑暗的裂痕，又会对从调查到友谊，再到他面对这起旧案重现的整个过程产生什么影响？

sentences.en: I figured it out as I went.
sentences.zh: 我是边写边想出来的。

sentences.en: Is that your normal process?
sentences.zh: 这是你通常的创作流程吗？

sentences.en: Is that how you've continued to write these books?
sentences.zh: 你一直以来都是这样写这些书的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实是这样。

sentences.en: Like, I don't usually know who done it when I go into writing a book.
sentences.zh: 比如，我开始写一本书时，通常并不知道凶手是谁。

sentences.en: And I'm, no, but I'm really, I'm envious of the authors who do.
sentences.zh: 不，但我真的很羡慕那些知道凶手是谁的作者。

sentences.en: I know writers who have every chapter outlined before they start.
sentences.zh: 我认识一些作家，他们在动笔前就已经列好了每一章的大纲。

sentences.en: And the joy of that is, you know, there's a book in there.
sentences.zh: 那样做的好处是，你知道书就在那里。

sentences.en: And I don't.
sentences.zh: 而我不是。

sentences.en: I'm diving in.
sentences.zh: 我直接跳进水里。

sentences.en: The swimming pool could be empty.
sentences.zh: 游泳池里可能根本没水。

sentences.en: I could just hit my head on the bottom and go, oh, oh, there was no book there.
sentences.zh: 我可能会一头撞在池底，然后心想，噢，原来根本没书。

sentences.en: But I think it has pluses and minuses.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这种方式有利有弊。

sentences.en: The minus being there's an awful lot of rewriting.
sentences.zh: 弊端就是需要大量的重写。

sentences.en: When you're halfway through chapter seven and you go, oh, my God, this person did that.
sentences.zh: 当你写到第七章的一半时，突然发现，天哪，原来是这个人干的。

sentences.en: And you have to go back and rewrite to strengthen that up and put it in its correct place.
sentences.zh: 然后你必须回头重写，以加强逻辑，并将其放在正确的位置。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, there's a sense of excitement that I get when I'm writing.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，我在写作时会有一种兴奋感。

sentences.en: And something's a discovery and something's new.
sentences.zh: 一切都是一种发现，一切都是新鲜的。

sentences.en: And I'm getting to know the characters as I go.
sentences.zh: 我是在写作的过程中逐渐了解角色的。

sentences.en: So I'm hoping that the plus side of this way of writing is that some of that communicates itself to the reader.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望这种写作方式的优点是，能将这种感觉传达给读者。

sentences.en: No, I mean, it definitely does.
sentences.zh: 不，我是说，这绝对能传达出来。

sentences.en: But there is so much risk in it.
sentences.zh: 但其中也蕴含着巨大的风险。

sentences.en: I wonder if there's any time where you've done this and you've kind of been like, I don't actually know if I'm going to be able to do it this time.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，有没有哪次你这样做的时候，心里会想，我真的不知道这次我能不能写出来。

sentences.en: There was only one time there.
sentences.zh: 只有过一次。

sentences.en: I mean, there's always a point about two thirds of the way through the book where you're like, yeah, this doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 我是说，写书写到三分之二的时候，总会有一个时刻让你觉得，完了，这行不通。

sentences.en: This sucks.
sentences.zh: 这太烂了。

sentences.en: All of this sucks.
sentences.zh: 这一切都糟透了。

sentences.en: I'm going to go back to being a broke actor living in a garret.
sentences.zh: 我还是回去当个住在阁楼里的穷演员吧。

sentences.en: But only once when I was writing The Trespasser, and it was very early on, I was about 2,000 words in.
sentences.zh: 但只有一次，是在写《入侵者》（The Trespasser）的时候，那是很早期的阶段，我大概写了2000字。

sentences.en: And I went, I don't feel like this is going much of anywhere.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得，这故事好像哪儿也去不了。

sentences.en: And I went for a long walk with my husband, who's very good at the structural stuff.
sentences.zh: 于是我和丈夫去散了长步，他非常擅长处理结构方面的问题。

sentences.en: And he went, well, what are the bits of this that you actually really, really want to write about?
sentences.zh: 他问我，你真正最想写的部分是什么？

sentences.en: How much of this do you really want?
sentences.zh: 你到底有多想要这些内容？

sentences.en: And I pared it back to about two or three elements and went, you know what, actually the rest, no, it is those two or three elements.
sentences.zh: 我把它删减到只剩两三个核心要素，然后发现，你知道吗，剩下的其实都不重要，关键就是那两三个要素。

sentences.en: He went, okay, keep those, start over.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，保留那些，重新开始。

sentences.en: And he was right, and I did.
sentences.zh: 他是对的，我也确实那样做了。

sentences.en: But I was lucky that it was very early on.
sentences.zh: 但我很幸运，那是在非常早期的阶段。

sentences.en: I wasn't like three quarters of the way through and went, oh, yeah, there's no ending.
sentences.zh: 我没有写到四分之三的时候才发现，噢，天哪，这书没结局。

sentences.en: I'm going to have to start over.
sentences.zh: 我得重头再来。

sentences.en: I'm honestly amazed at the idea that you kind of approach these books like a detective yourself, trying to figure out what happens.
sentences.zh: 老实说，你像侦探一样去构思这些书，试图找出真相，这让我感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: How do you make sure that you're not following a storyline down a rabbit hole?
sentences.zh: 你是如何确保自己不会在故事情节中钻牛角尖的？

sentences.en: Like, how do you stay focused if you're figuring it out as it happens?
sentences.zh: 如果你是边写边想，你是如何保持专注的？

sentences.en: And I think this is one of the reasons I write mystery, because it's quite good at keeping you on track, because it comes with a framework.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是我写悬疑小说的原因之一，因为它很擅长让你保持在正轨上，因为它自带框架。

sentences.en: It comes with A kills B, C finds out who did it.
sentences.zh: 它自带“A杀了B，C找出凶手”的模式。

sentences.en: And you can play with that.
sentences.zh: 你可以利用这个框架。

sentences.en: You can, you know, undermine that, play with it, turn it around inside out.
sentences.zh: 你可以推翻它、玩弄它、把它彻底颠覆。

sentences.en: But that's the basic framework.
sentences.zh: 但这就是基本框架。

sentences.en: And so it has a shape.
sentences.zh: 所以它有一个形状。

sentences.en: It has a natural ending, a mystery book does.
sentences.zh: 悬疑小说有一个自然的结局。

sentences.en: And I think that's why I write mystery and what keeps me on track, because you can't just wander off.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是我写悬疑小说的原因，也是让我不偏离轨道的原因，因为你不能随意乱写。

sentences.en: On someone's entire life story.
sentences.zh: 写进某人完整的人生故事里。

sentences.en: Anything you're writing has to feed, not just into the character, not just into the themes, but also into that story drive towards the moment when there's some form of closure.
sentences.zh: 你写的任何东西都必须服务于故事，不仅是服务于角色，不仅是服务于主题，还要服务于那个推向结局时刻的动力。

sentences.en: And I think that's my main way of keeping myself on track.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是我保持不偏离轨道的主要方法。

sentences.en: Do you ever feel hemmed in by that basic convention, A kills B, C finds out?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾感到被“A杀了B，C找出凶手”这种基本套路所束缚？

sentences.en: I mean, I understand you're saying there's a way in which it's freeing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我明白你的意思，这种套路在某种程度上也是一种解放。

sentences.en: It allows you to kind of explore these characters expansively and stay on track.
sentences.zh: 它让你能够广阔地探索这些角色，同时保持在正轨上。

sentences.en: But I wonder if it creates these expectations from readers that may feel limiting at times.
sentences.zh: 但我好奇这是否会给读者带来某种预期，从而让你感到受限？

sentences.en: Not really, for two reasons.
sentences.zh: 其实不会，有两个原因。

sentences.en: One of which is maybe better than the other.
sentences.zh: 其中一个原因可能比另一个更好。

sentences.en: The better one is there's so much variation within that.
sentences.zh: 更好的那个原因是，在这个框架内有太多的变化空间。

sentences.en: Because the real question in most mysteries, I don't think it is whodunit.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为大多数悬疑小说里，真正的问题并不是“谁是凶手”。

sentences.en: That's not the big question.
sentences.zh: 那不是最大的问题。

sentences.en: The big question is, what impact does this have on the characters?
sentences.zh: 最大的问题是，这对角色有什么影响？

sentences.en: What does it mean for the society in which it happens?
sentences.zh: 这对故事发生的社会意味着什么？

sentences.en: How are they going to deal with this revelation?
sentences.zh: 他们将如何面对这个真相？

sentences.en: How will they process it?
sentences.zh: 他们将如何消化它？

sentences.en: Will it change them?
sentences.zh: 这会改变他们吗？

sentences.en: Will it change their world or them as individuals?
sentences.zh: 这会改变他们的世界或他们个人吗？

sentences.en: So whodunit is the smallest question, I think, in most thrillers.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，在大多数惊悚小说中，“谁是凶手”反而是最小的问题。

sentences.en: And the other reason is that, I mean, as In the Woods shows, sometimes I just go, yeah, no, that's not the big question.
sentences.zh: 另一个原因是，正如《神秘森林》（In the Woods）所展示的那样，有时我就是会想，好吧，那不是最大的问题。

sentences.en: And so there's not going to be an answer.
sentences.zh: 所以它不会有一个答案。

sentences.en: I've only done it that once, but I don't think that was the big question.
sentences.zh: 我只那样做过一次，但我不认为那是最大的问题。

sentences.en: In In the Woods, it's will this character be able to move past that damage, which is answered.
sentences.zh: 在《神秘森林》中，核心问题是这个角色能否走出那段创伤，而这个问题是有答案的。

sentences.en: Yes, we should say for people who may not have read this book, and this is not, I don't think,
sentences.zh: 是的，我们应该对那些可能还没读过这本书的人说，我不认为这算剧透，

sentences.en: a spoiler, but you burst onto the scene with this debut that essentially set up this crazy premise, which you laid out, three kids disappear into the woods, one emerges.
sentences.zh: 你凭借这部处女作一举成名，它设定了一个疯狂的前提，正如你所说，三个孩子走进森林，只有一个走了出来。

sentences.en: And then the whole book proceeds, and it's not really about figuring out what happened at that moment.
sentences.zh: 然后整本书继续推进，它其实并不是关于找出那一刻发生了什么。

sentences.en: It's about a different crime, and it remains unsolved.
sentences.zh: 它是关于另一桩罪案，而且它始终未解。

sentences.en: I'm sure you still get many, many questions from people who ask you whether you're ever going to tell us.
sentences.zh: 我相信你仍然会收到很多读者的提问，问你是否会告诉我们真相。

sentences.en: Yeah, and no, I don't think I am going to come back to that, because I think the big questions of that book were answered.
sentences.zh: 是的，不，我想我不会再回到那个话题了，因为我认为那本书的核心问题已经得到了解答。

sentences.en: And I didn't think about it at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时我并没有多想。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: So should I?
sentences.zh: 那我应该写吗？

sentences.en: But I couldn't really do that without being very false to the character, without turning him at the last minute in the book into somebody different.
sentences.zh: 但我无法在不背叛角色的情况下做到这一点，不能在书的最后一刻把他变成另一个人。

sentences.en: And that felt cheap and cheesy, and I wasn't going to do that, so I just went, okay, some people will be justifiably really annoyed with this ending, because it does not fit the
sentences.zh: 那感觉很廉价、很俗套，我不会那样做，所以我只是想，好吧，有些人会因为这个结局而感到非常恼火，这是合理的，因为它不符合

sentences.en: conventions that they went in expecting, and they are going to feel cheated, and that's fair enough.
sentences.zh: 他们预期的套路，他们会觉得被欺骗了，这很正常。

sentences.en: But there will be other readers who would feel equally cheated if I turned the character into someone else for the sake of having a clean answer.
sentences.zh: 但也会有其他读者，如果我为了给出一个干净利落的答案而把角色变成另一个人，他们同样会感到被欺骗。

sentences.en: So I'm just going to go with what I think is the right ending for the book, and keep my fingers crossed.
sentences.zh: 所以我打算坚持我认为对这本书来说正确的结局，并祈祷好运。

sentences.en: Okay, not to harp on it, but do you, in your heart of hearts, know what happened?
sentences.zh: 好的，不是想纠结这个问题，但在你的内心深处，你知道发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I've got a pretty clear idea.
sentences.zh: 是的，我有一个相当清晰的想法。

sentences.en: Okay, all right, we'll leave it at that.
sentences.zh: 好的，好吧，我们就此打住。

sentences.en: I'm one of those readers that was fully satisfied.
sentences.zh: 我就是那些感到完全满足的读者之一。

sentences.en: We're going to take a quick break, and when we come back, I want to talk about your approach to these great characters that you write.
sentences.zh: 我们要休息一下，回来后，我想谈谈你处理这些伟大角色的方式。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I want to talk about your approach to your characters.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈你处理角色的方式。

sentences.en: A lot of thriller writers have written series of books that are centered around one character.
sentences.zh: 很多惊悚小说作家都写过以同一个角色为中心的系列丛书。

sentences.en: James Patterson has Alex Cross.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·帕特森（James Patterson）有亚历克斯·克罗斯（Alex Cross）。

sentences.en: Lee Child has Jack Reacher.
sentences.zh: 李·查德（Lee Child）有杰克·雷彻（Jack Reacher）。

sentences.en: Your Dublin Murder Squad books center on different characters who are all connected, but they have
sentences.zh: 你的《都柏林谋杀案》（Dublin Murder Squad）系列以不同的角色为中心，他们之间都有联系，但他们有

sentences.en: different stories, different ticks, different quirks, and different damage, honestly.
sentences.zh: 不同的故事、不同的怪癖、不同的性格缺陷，说实话。

sentences.en: They're often deeply flawed narrators, sometimes with memory problems, and the result in that
sentences.zh: 他们通常是有严重缺陷的叙述者，有时还有记忆问题，结果就是

sentences.en: series is that you don't, as a reader, have this stable, all-knowing authority soothingly solving a crime.
sentences.zh: 作为读者，你没有一个稳定的、全知全能的权威来安抚性地解决案件。

sentences.en: You have a rotating cast of people searching alongside you who you may or may not trust all the time.
sentences.zh: 你有一群轮换的角色和你一起寻找真相，你可能并不总是信任他们。

sentences.en: Why did you take that approach?
sentences.zh: 你为什么采取这种方式？

sentences.en: I thought about it a lot when I finished In the Woods and was thinking, oh my God, somebody might someday want a second book.
sentences.zh: 我在写完《神秘森林》后想了很多，心想，天哪，也许有一天有人会想要第二本书。

sentences.en: I should probably think about that.
sentences.zh: 我大概应该考虑一下这个问题。

sentences.en: I love those series that you talk about.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢你提到的那些系列。

sentences.en: You know, P.D.
sentences.zh: 你知道，P.D.

sentences.en: James has Adam Dalgleish, and I love series like that, where you follow one detective through kind of the different cases and the ups and downs of his or her life.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯（P.D. James）有亚当·达格利什（Adam Dalgleish），我喜欢那样的系列，你跟随一位侦探经历各种案件，以及他或她生活中的起起落落。

sentences.en: But the thing is, that's not what I was interested in writing.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，那不是我想写的东西。

sentences.en: Because I was interested in writing about a case that hits a detective right on their most vulnerable point, and that changes them as a person, that makes them confront the things
sentences.zh: 因为我想写的是一个案件，它击中了侦探最脆弱的地方，这改变了他们的人格，让他们不得不面对

sentences.en: that are most difficult and most crucial within their own mind.
sentences.zh: 自己内心最困难、最关键的东西。

sentences.en: And there's a limit to how many cases one person can have that are huge turning points in their own life.
sentences.zh: 一个人一生中能经历多少次巨大的转折点案件是有限的。

sentences.en: So I was like, okay, I can either keep dumping the same poor guy with massive turning points, in which case he is going to be like locked up in a straitjacket by book three.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想，好吧，我要么继续让同一个可怜人不断遭遇巨大的转折点，那样的话，到第三本书他可能就被关进精神病院了。

sentences.en: Or I can shift from detective to detective, picking up each one at the moment when they have that case that's a turning point that will affect the way the rest of their whole
sentences.zh: 要么我可以从一个侦探换到另一个侦探，在他们遇到那个会影响他们余生走向的转折点案件时切入。

sentences.en: life plays out.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定这样做，把这些书像链条一样连接起来。

sentences.en: So I decided to do that and kind of chain link the books together.
sentences.zh: 所以某个人可能是第三本书里的一个小角色，然后成为第四本书的叙述者。

sentences.en: So somebody might be a minor character in book three and then the narrator in book four.
sentences.zh: 但你是在他们遇到重大转折点案件的时刻切入他们的故事。

sentences.en: But you're picking them up at the point where something massive, a crossroads case has hit them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你读这些书时，你会发现自己对理解、了解或弄清楚侦探的兴趣，

sentences.en: You know, what happens as you're reading these things is that you find yourself about as interested in understanding or knowing or figuring out the detective as you do about
sentences.zh: 几乎和你对找出悬疑案件、罪行、凶手的答案一样浓厚。

sentences.en: finding out the answer to the mystery, the crime, the killer.
sentences.zh: 太棒了，很好。

sentences.en: Great, good.
sentences.zh: 听起来这就是重点。

sentences.en: It sounds like that's the point.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 是的，真的是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah, it really is.
sentences.zh: 我是说，对我来说，最大的谜团就是人，以及他们是如何运作的，当事情变得复杂、困难时，他们是如何度过一生的。

sentences.en: I mean, for me, that is the big mystery is people and how they work and how they move through life when things get complicated, when things are difficult.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是悬疑小说做得非常好的地方。

sentences.en: I think that's what mystery does really well.
sentences.zh: 因为在“谁杀了这个人”这个框架之上，你还有那么多关于人性的问题

sentences.en: Because on that framework of, you know, who killed this person, you've got so many questions
sentences.zh: 等待着被探索。

sentences.en: right there asking to be explored about people's minds.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一个人是如何从一个正常人变成杀人犯的？

sentences.en: You know, how does someone get from being a normal human being to being a murderer?
sentences.zh: 是什么驱使他们走到那一步？

sentences.en: What takes them there?
sentences.zh: 这对调查人员、周围的人、嫌疑人有什么影响？

sentences.en: What effects does this have on the people who investigate, the people who are all around it, the people who are suspects?
sentences.zh: 这些都是关于人类心理深处的重大课题。

sentences.en: These are huge things about like the depths of the human psyche.
sentences.zh: 什么样的黑暗面创造了谋杀，无论是在社会层面还是在个人的内心深处？

sentences.en: What dark places create a murder, both in society and the dark places of the individual?
sentences.zh: 我认为这些问题非常迷人，比“谁干的”这种容易回答的黑白分明的问题有趣得多。

sentences.en: I think those are fascinating and much more interesting than the easily answered black and white question of who did this?
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那些永远不会有完全答案的问题，但悬疑小说为我们提供了一种至少可以去探索它们的方式。

sentences.en: I like the questions that will never be fully answered, but mystery gives us a way to at least explore them.
sentences.zh: 塔娜（Tana），我在读你的书时有一种感觉，我想很多人也有同感，那就是你有一种方式

sentences.en: Tana, something I feel reading you, I think a lot of people do, is that you have this way
sentences.zh: 不仅是彻底探索人，探索人类本身，而且是彻底探索地方，探索历史中特定的

sentences.en: of not just thoroughly exploring people, human beings, but thoroughly exploring places, particular
sentences.zh: 时刻，以及所有施加在它们身上的政治和社会力量。

sentences.en: moments in history with all the political and social forces that bear down on them.
sentences.zh: 在《破碎港湾》（Broken Harbor）中，那起罪案，那个谜团，完全是由爱尔兰在金融危机中挣扎的背景所塑造的。

sentences.en: In Broken Harbor, that crime, the mystery there, it's entirely shaped by the setting of Ireland reeling from the financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所追求的。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, is that part of how you develop the ideas for your stories?
sentences.zh: 我想问一下，这是否是你构思故事灵感的一部分？

sentences.en: Do they grow out of that specific times and geographical places?
sentences.zh: 它们是源于特定的时代和地理位置吗？

sentences.en: It's not usually on purpose.
sentences.zh: 通常不是刻意的。

sentences.en: I just, I think that this genre is kind of uniquely suited to doing that.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得，这种类型文学在处理这类题材上有着独特的优势。

sentences.en: Because when you're dealing with a murder, which mystery often does, you're dealing with huge stuff with the, you know, murder is different in every time and place.
sentences.zh: 因为当你处理谋杀案时——悬疑小说经常涉及这一点——你处理的是宏大的议题，你知道，谋杀在不同的时间和地点有着不同的含义。

sentences.en: It happens everywhere, but it happens for different reasons in different times and places.
sentences.zh: 它随处可见，但在不同的时间和地点，发生的原因各不相同。

sentences.en: You will not have a murder over ownership of a piece of land among a nomadic tribe.
sentences.zh: 你不会在游牧部落中因为土地所有权问题而发生谋杀案。

sentences.en: It's just, that's not a priority to them.
sentences.zh: 那对他们来说根本不是优先事项。

sentences.en: But you would have it in rural Ireland and have had many times.
sentences.zh: 但在爱尔兰农村，这种情况却发生过很多次。

sentences.en: So the minute you have a murder, you're into exploring what are the priorities for this society?
sentences.zh: 所以，一旦发生谋杀案，你就在探索：这个社会的优先事项是什么？

sentences.en: What are the things that are so crucial and so highly emotionally charged that someone will kill over them?
sentences.zh: 究竟是什么事情如此关键，又如此牵动情绪，以至于有人会为此杀人？

sentences.en: Or what are the fears that are so intense, you know, that someone will kill because of this fear?
sentences.zh: 或者说，是什么样的恐惧如此强烈，以至于有人会因为这种恐惧而杀人？

sentences.en: And those are shaped by the society.
sentences.zh: 而这些都是由社会塑造的。

sentences.en: So you start writing, you know, you're going to be there.
sentences.zh: 所以当你开始写作时，你知道，你注定会身处其中。

sentences.en: You're going to be diving into that, whether you intend to or not.
sentences.zh: 无论你是否有意，你都会深入挖掘这些问题。

sentences.en: And I think that's where I land.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是我最终落脚的地方。

sentences.en: You're drawn like a magnet to those moments of maximum tension because, precisely because they're the kinds of things people would kill over.
sentences.zh: 你会像磁铁一样被吸引到那些极度紧张的时刻，恰恰是因为它们是人们会为此杀人的那种事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they're shaped.
sentences.zh: 而且它们是被塑造出来的。

sentences.en: You're talking about society.
sentences.zh: 你在谈论社会。

sentences.en: When you say somebody killed for this in a murder, you are saying something about that time and place, whether you intended to or not.
sentences.zh: 当你提到某人在谋杀案中因为这个原因杀人时，无论你是否有意，你都在传达关于那个时代和地点的信息。

sentences.en: So that honestly unlocked for me part of the reason why your work is so compelling, because it sounds like you see mystery everywhere.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这让我明白了为什么你的作品如此引人入胜，因为听起来你随处都能看到悬疑。

sentences.en: You see mystery in who people are.
sentences.zh: 你在人们的本质中看到了悬疑。

sentences.en: You see mystery in the things that happen in these small towns that are cut off from the kind of big cities.
sentences.zh: 你在那些远离大城市的小镇所发生的事情中看到了悬疑。

sentences.en: And you kind of invite people to think of their world as full of these mysteries that they could be engaging with, solving, or helping to bring light to.
sentences.zh: 你邀请人们去思考，他们的世界充满了这些可以参与、解决或协助揭示真相的谜团。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这一点。

sentences.en: I would love that.
sentences.zh: 我也很喜欢。

sentences.en: Because I think one of the things that makes us human is that we love mysteries.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为人类之所以为人，原因之一就是我们热爱谜团。

sentences.en: Like, animals aren't the same way.
sentences.zh: 比如，动物就不会这样。

sentences.en: Like, you know, you've got a cat or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你养了只猫之类的。

sentences.en: The cat will check something out.
sentences.zh: 猫会去查看某样东西。

sentences.en: Is it a box that I can sit in?
sentences.zh: 这是个我可以坐进去的盒子吗？

sentences.en: Can I eat it?
sentences.zh: 我能吃它吗？

sentences.en: Should I be scared of it?
sentences.zh: 我该怕它吗？

sentences.en: No, okay, fine, I'm not interested anymore.
sentences.zh: 不，好吧，没兴趣了。

sentences.en: But humans will always, we're not just interested in the solution to the mystery.
sentences.zh: 但人类总是这样，我们不仅仅对谜团的答案感兴趣。

sentences.en: It's not just the answer to the question that fascinates us.
sentences.zh: 让我们着迷的不仅仅是问题的答案。

sentences.en: It's the mystery itself.
sentences.zh: 而是谜团本身。

sentences.en: It's the fact that there is something out there that's a huge question mark and that needs exploring and that the process of exploring it is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 事实是，世界上存在着巨大的未知，需要去探索，而探索的过程本身就令人着迷。

sentences.en: The fact that we could go on exploring and find layers of answers and never get to the core answer, we're fascinated by that.
sentences.zh: 我们能够不断探索，发现层层答案，却永远无法触及核心答案，我们对此感到着迷。

sentences.en: Tana, people often talk about your work as kind of riding the border between literary and genre fiction.
sentences.zh: 塔娜，人们常说你的作品游走在纯文学和类型小说之间。

sentences.en: I wonder what you think about that.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你怎么看？

sentences.en: What space do you locate your work in?
sentences.zh: 你将自己的作品定位在什么空间？

sentences.en: See, I don't believe in that border anyway.
sentences.zh: 你看，我本来就不相信有那条界限。

sentences.en: I don't think there is a border.
sentences.zh: 我不认为存在什么界限。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think, I mean, if you look at that list, that wonderful list of the 50 best thrillers, it kind of shatters the idea that there is such a thing as a thriller.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，如果你看看那份名单，那份精彩的“50部最佳惊悚小说”名单，它打破了“惊悚小说”这一概念的固有定义。

sentences.en: Because the books on that are so different.
sentences.zh: 因为名单上的书差异太大了。

sentences.en: You've got, you know, you've got the Da Vinci Code, you've got, you know, Mystic River is on there, you have the Goldfinch, you have Room.
sentences.zh: 你有《达芬奇密码》，有《神秘河》，有《金翅雀》，还有《房间》。

sentences.en: There is no world in which those books are all the same kind of book.
sentences.zh: 在任何情况下，这些书都不可能被归为同一种书。

sentences.en: Part of what you're saying is, it's not just that you don't believe in the border, it sounds like readers don't really see that border either.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说的一部分意思是，不仅你不相信这条界限，听起来读者们也并不真的认为存在这条界限。

sentences.en: I want to talk about this list, the 50 best thrillers of the century that the Times just put out.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈这份《泰晤士报》刚刚发布的“本世纪50部最佳惊悚小说”名单。

sentences.en: You're talking a little bit about this.
sentences.zh: 你刚才稍微提到了这一点。

sentences.en: What did you think of it?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看？

sentences.en: What were your impressions when you saw it?
sentences.zh: 当你看到它时，你的印象是什么？

sentences.en: That was my first impression, is that for a list of the 50 best thrillers, it makes it pretty clear that there is no definition of a thriller.
sentences.zh: 我的第一印象是，对于一份“50部最佳惊悚小说”的名单来说，它清楚地表明了惊悚小说根本没有定义。

sentences.en: Because you look at these, and while I can see why each of them is on the list, I think
sentences.zh: 因为你看看这些书，虽然我能理解它们为什么会上榜，但我认为……

sentences.en: it's really hard to go, to say with any conviction that they all belong in the same category.
sentences.zh: 很难坚定地说它们都属于同一个类别。

sentences.en: And these are wonderful books, but they approach the concept of the thrillers so differently.
sentences.zh: 这些都是很棒的书，但它们处理“惊悚”这一概念的方式截然不同。

sentences.en: You know, Room, Emma Donoghue's Room, doesn't seem to me to be particularly shaped in any way by the conventions that we would consider to hold for a thriller or a mystery.
sentences.zh: 你知道，《房间》，艾玛·多诺霍的《房间》，在我看来，它似乎并没有受到我们认为适用于惊悚或悬疑小说的那些惯例的任何影响。

sentences.en: And the same for, you know, the Goldfinch.
sentences.zh: 《金翅雀》也是如此。

sentences.en: It plays with the whole heist idea, but it doesn't seem to in any way be shaped by the conventions.
sentences.zh: 它玩弄了整个抢劫题材的构思，但它似乎并没有受到任何惯例的束缚。

sentences.en: It just uses them to have fun with as sort of lovely little icings.
sentences.zh: 它只是把这些当作一种有趣的装饰。

sentences.en: So I think this would be, that was the first thing I thought of when I saw this liSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，这就是我看到这份名单时想到的第一件事。

sentences.en: More than a list of 50 best thrillers, it's a list of 50 great fun ways to engage with the concept that there is such a thing as a thriller.
sentences.zh: 与其说这是一份50部最佳惊悚小说名单，不如说这是一份50种探索“惊悚小说”这一概念的有趣方式的清单。

sentences.en: And, okay, I have to ask, the way that this was constructed, these ballots were sent out, and the Times didn't tell anybody, you know, these are the parameters for what a thriller
sentences.zh: 好吧，我必须问一下，这份名单的制作方式是寄出选票，而《泰晤士报》并没有告诉任何人，你知道，什么是惊悚小说的参数。

sentences.en: is.
So really, it is a reflection of what people think of when they think of thrillers.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实反映了人们在想到惊悚小说时会想到什么。

sentences.en: And I want to know what you think people did when they went to think of it.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你认为人们在思考时做了什么。

sentences.en: Was it a feeling they tried to conjure and then pick the books that most match that feeling of kind of tension, suspense, catharsis?
sentences.zh: 他们是试图唤起一种感觉，然后挑选出最符合那种紧张、悬疑、宣泄感的书吗？

sentences.en: All I can say is I got nine books into my ballot and then forgot to send it in, so I can only say what I did when I was trying to write them out.
sentences.zh: 我只能说，我填了九本书就忘了寄出去了，所以我只能说我在写名单时做了什么。

sentences.en: I'm an idiot.
sentences.zh: 我是个白痴。

sentences.en: When I was trying to write them out, I can only say what I did, which was, I went for my ten favorite books that I could, by any stretch of the imagination, claim worth for theirs.
sentences.zh: 当我在写名单时，我只能说我做了什么，那就是我选了我最喜欢的十本书，只要发挥一点想象力，我都能声称它们值得上榜。

sentences.en: Okay, I have to ask, can we hear the lost ballot?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我必须问，我们能听听那份丢失的选票吗？

sentences.en: What were, what are the books that you would put on this list if you could, if we now gave you the time to submit it?
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，如果你现在有时间提交，你会把哪些书放进这份名单？

sentences.en: I can't remember because I kept finding ones and going, crap, that wasn't 21st century, was it?
sentences.zh: 我不记得了，因为我一直在找书，然后发现：糟了，那不是21世纪的书，对吧？

sentences.en: But I know Mystic River and Gone Girl, which ended up being the top two, they were in fact on there.
sentences.zh: 但我知道《神秘河》和《消失的爱人》，它们最终排名前二，它们确实在名单上。

sentences.en: Winter's Bone was in there.
sentences.zh: 《冬天的骨头》也在里面。

sentences.en: The Yiddish Policemen's Union, I know it was in there, but I can't remember whether it turned out to be too early or not.
sentences.zh: 《犹太警察工会》，我知道它在里面，但我记不清它是不是出版太早了。

sentences.en: I love that book.
sentences.zh: 我爱那本书。

sentences.en: That is an absolute beauty of a book.
sentences.zh: 那绝对是一本杰作。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I love that book.
sentences.zh: 我爱那本书。

sentences.en: What did you love about that book?
sentences.zh: 你喜欢那本书的什么？

sentences.en: What about it, you know, or any of the books, but what reaches your upper echelon?
sentences.zh: 关于它，或者任何书，是什么让你觉得它们达到了顶尖水平？

sentences.en: Well, that one in particular, it has everything.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那本书特别之处在于，它应有尽有。

sentences.en: Like, it is a noir, and it just dives joyfully into all of the noir tropes.
sentences.zh: 它是一部黑色小说，它愉快地沉浸在所有的黑色电影桥段中。

sentences.en: He writes so beautifully, my God, the things he does with language, just about any sentence.
sentences.zh: 他写得太美了，天哪，他在语言上的造诣，几乎每一句话都是如此。

sentences.en: You could go to somebody, listen to this, listen to this, how beautiful this is.
sentences.zh: 你可以找个人说：听着，听着，这有多美。

sentences.en: His characterization is incredible.
sentences.zh: 他的人物刻画令人难以置信。

sentences.en: He can give you one sentence and just slice straight to the heart of a character.
sentences.zh: 他能用一句话就直击人物的内心。

sentences.en: And he can turn on a dime between being so funny and being so moving and being so dark.
sentences.zh: 他能在幽默、动人和黑暗之间瞬间切换。

sentences.en: And the plot just keeps you going the whole way.
sentences.zh: 而且情节让你全程欲罢不能。

sentences.en: So I think it was that.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为就是这些。

sentences.en: It was, this just hits all my favorite things in a book.
sentences.zh: 它击中了我喜欢一本书的所有要素。

sentences.en: And it revels in the genre without ever being constrained by it.
sentences.zh: 它沉浸在类型文学中，却从未被其束缚。

sentences.en: Okay, do you have recommendations for our listeners?
sentences.zh: 好的，你有什么推荐给我们的听众吗？

sentences.en: They can be thrillers or not.
sentences.zh: 可以是惊悚小说，也可以不是。

sentences.en: They don't have to be in the 21st century, but things that you would tell people to drop everything and read right now.
sentences.zh: 不一定要是21世纪的作品，但有没有什么书是你觉得人们应该放下一切立刻去读的？

sentences.en: Okay, if I start jabbering, do stop me because there are so many books.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果我开始喋喋不休，一定要阻止我，因为好书太多了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I won't.
sentences.zh: 我不会的。

sentences.en: Most recently, Northwoods by Daniel Mason, which is so hard to describe because it is
sentences.zh: 最近读的是丹尼尔·梅森的《北林》，很难描述它，因为它讲述的是……

sentences.en: the story of a piece of land in New England over 400 years through, you know, diaries, ballads, narratives, letters, whatever you want.
sentences.zh: 新英格兰一片土地400年的故事，通过日记、民谣、叙事、信件，随你怎么说。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: It's enchanted.
sentences.zh: 它充满魔力。

sentences.en: Lonesome Dove.
sentences.zh: 《孤鸽镇》。

sentences.en: It's an incredible book.
sentences.zh: 这是一本不可思议的书。

sentences.en: It's the story of a bunch of guys in the 1870s taking a cattle drive from Texas to Montana.
sentences.zh: 讲述了19世纪70年代一群人从德克萨斯州赶牛到蒙大拿州的故事。

sentences.en: And it is, it's a slow start, but it's wonderful for character, for atmosphere, for everything.
sentences.zh: 开头有点慢，但在人物塑造、氛围营造等方面都很棒。

sentences.en: The Secret History, I love it.
sentences.zh: 《校园秘史》，我爱死它了。

sentences.en: Some people, I know it's love it or hate it, but I adore it.
sentences.zh: 有些人，我知道它是那种让人爱恨分明的书，但我崇拜它。

sentences.en: It's love it over here.
sentences.zh: 这里也是爱它的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Oh, God, the characterization, the writing.
sentences.zh: 天哪，那人物刻画，那文笔。

sentences.en: I would read anything she wrote.
sentences.zh: 她写的任何东西我都会读。

sentences.en: And that big reveal scene, the house could have burned down around me during the big reveal scene and I would not have noticed it the first time I read that book.
sentences.zh: 还有那个大揭秘场景，第一次读那本书时，即使房子在我周围烧起来，我也不会注意到。

sentences.en: OK, I must ask you something that our thrillers columnist, Sarah Lyle, insisted I ask and that, honestly, I think millions of people want to know, which is, what are you up to next
sentences.zh: 好的，我必须问你一个我们的惊悚小说专栏作家莎拉·莱尔坚持要我问的问题，老实说，我认为数以百万计的人都想知道，那就是：你接下来在忙什么？

sentences.en: and when can we pre-order it?
sentences.zh: 什么时候可以预订？

sentences.en: It's a little bit weird.
sentences.zh: 有点奇怪。

sentences.en: It's a little different.
sentences.zh: 有点不同。

sentences.en: I've never written about COVID, if you notice.
sentences.zh: 如果你注意到了，我从未写过关于新冠的内容。

sentences.en: The searcher was handed in just before COVID started.
sentences.zh: 《搜寻者》是在新冠开始前交稿的。

sentences.en: So the hunter and the keeper were written during COVID.
sentences.zh: 所以《猎人》和《守门人》是在新冠期间写的。

sentences.en: But I never mentioned, there's no COVID in our decalty.
sentences.zh: 但我从未提及，我们的故事里没有新冠。

sentences.en: These people are not dealing with COVID.
sentences.zh: 这些人没有在处理新冠问题。

sentences.en: I'm not dealing with it.
sentences.zh: 我也没有在处理它。

sentences.en: Forget it.
sentences.zh: 忘掉它吧。

sentences.en: And people kept asking me, are you going to write about this?
sentences.zh: 人们一直问我：你会写这个吗？

sentences.en: I was like, no, I don't even want to do it.
sentences.zh: 我说：不，我甚至不想碰它。

sentences.en: Never mind, write about it.
sentences.zh: 更别提写它了。

sentences.en: But now, at this distance, I have ended up writing about it.
sentences.zh: 但现在，隔了一段时间，我最终还是写了它。

sentences.en: And this book is set on a road in a suburb of a small Irish city or town, where just as the lockdown hits, a woman and her two small daughters arrive on the road.
sentences.zh: 这本书设定在爱尔兰一个小城市或城镇郊区的一条路上，就在封锁开始时，一个女人带着她的两个小女儿来到了这条路上。

sentences.en: And over the course of the lockdown, the different people on the road realize that she may not be who she says she is.
sentences.zh: 在封锁期间，路上的不同人意识到，她可能不是她所说的那个人。

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: She may be here for a purpose, and that purpose may have effects on the entire balance of this little kind of tight-knit road.
sentences.zh: 她可能别有目的，而这个目的可能会对这条紧密相连的街道的整体平衡产生影响。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: When can I pre-order it?
sentences.zh: 我什么时候可以预订？

sentences.en: Most important question.
sentences.zh: 最重要的问题。

sentences.en: I should touch wood, all going well, and it is going well.
sentences.zh: 我得敲敲木头，一切顺利的话——而且确实很顺利。

sentences.en: It's fun to write.
sentences.zh: 写起来很有趣。

sentences.en: Be handing it in next time.
sentences.zh: 下次就交稿了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, I don't totally know what I'm going to do until then.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在那之前我还没完全想好要做什么。

sentences.en: Tana, thank you so much for coming on the show.
sentences.zh: 塔娜，非常感谢你来到节目中。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: Listen, thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 听着，非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: This was a joy.
sentences.zh: 这真是一次愉快的经历。

sentences.en: On Friday, The Times released the list of the 100 best thrillers of the century chosen by you, our readers.
sentences.zh: 周五，《泰晤士报》发布了由你们——我们的读者——选出的“本世纪100部最佳惊悚小说”名单。

sentences.en: And nine of Tana's 10 books were on that liSt.
sentences.zh: 而塔娜的10本书中有9本都在那份名单上。

sentences.en: Well done, guys.
sentences.zh: 干得好，各位。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Luke Vanderplug, with help from Alex Barron and Tina Antolini, and production assistance from Dahlia Haddad.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由卢克·范德普拉格制作，亚历克斯·巴伦和蒂娜·安托利尼提供协助，达莉亚·哈达德担任制作助理。

sentences.en: It was edited by Wendy Doerr and engineered by Rowan Nemisto.
sentences.zh: 节目由温迪·多尔剪辑，罗文·内米斯托负责工程。

sentences.en: It includes music by Dan Powell and Marion Lozano.
sentences.zh: 节目配乐由丹·鲍威尔和马里昂·洛萨诺创作。

sentences.en: That's it for the Sunday Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期周日日报的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Natalie Kittroweth.
sentences.zh: 我是娜塔莉·基特罗韦斯。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们将为您准备假日待客指南。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人们宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们需要全黑环境才能入睡吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我指的不是那种喝断片儿了才睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这可是个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物不耐受吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 欢迎在《纽约时报》App或您常用的播客平台收听《Wirecutter秀》。
